subject: MULTIPLY statement
notes: SR4 'When native arithmetic is in effect, the composite of operands ... is determined by using all of the operands in the statement.' (cite --check 14.9.26.3 OK). Unlike ADD/SUBTRACT GIVING (which exclude receivers per their SR1b), MULTIPLY passes the GIVING receivers into the composite. Probe CP.cob: 9(5) x 9(5) GIVING 9(20)V9(11) = 31 accepted; MULTIPLY V9(12) BY 9(20) -> COBOL0805 (32); MULTIPLY 0.000000000001 BY B GIVING 9(20) -> 0805 (32, GIVING counted); not applied under STANDARD-DECIMAL (SD.cob). Note (14.7.7's subject, not this row): the cap is 31 at every edition, including --std 85, a documented reading in CheckComposite. No MULTIPLY composite negative golden (l1-add-composite-over-31 is ADD) -> test-needed.
